findings.text: The first sentence tells a newcomer what Athena is: open-source, written in Rust, and it turns a request into a code change. So the 'what is it' question is answered right away.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: This is Athena's own URL, yet almost the whole page is about a different project, firstmate. Athena gets three short header paragraphs. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets little more than that before 40+ cards and claims about firstmate.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and the header lede "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project..."

findings.text: The page says Athena's job is to make changes, then shows a read-only study. It never says how a study relates to making changes, or whether studies are a main feature or only a demonstration. A newcomer is left unsure what Athena is mainly for.
findings.source: header lede: "turns a short request into a change to a code repository" vs. "A study is Athena's written reading of another software project"

findings.text: The page names cross-model checking and cost records as Athena's selling points but shows neither for this study. No checker, model or cost appears anywhere on the page, so the newcomer cannot see these features in action.
findings.source: header lede: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost"

findings.text: The 'why it matters' case is concrete and works: every statement links to a claim, and every claim links to exact file lines at a pinned commit. A newcomer can check this themselves by clicking through.
findings.source: header lede: "Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end." and the Claims and sources section

findings.text: This is insider detail. A newcomer does not know which repository has a studies/ folder, or why the folder name matters on a first visit.
findings.source: header lede: "is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"

findings.text: The next step is clear and is linked from the header as well. But it only points to GitHub: the page gives no install command and no example request, so the newcomer has to leave the page to learn how to start.
findings.source: Next steps: "Learn about Athena, and how to install and try it: https://github.com/doodla/athena"

findings.text: The term 'wake' is never defined, so this definition goes in a circle. Other words in the cards and claims are also never explained, such as 'harness pin', 'standing charter', 'crewmates', 'endpoint' and 'captain-held inventory'.
findings.source: Glossary: "stale wake — A wake after which the agent inspects a worker that may have stopped, looped or gone quiet."

findings.text: The finding ids skip f2 with no explanation. A careful reader may wonder whether a finding was left out.

For a reader who wants to learn firstmate, the Start here section is well organised. Terms are defined before they are used, there is a numbered walk-through of one piece of work, and there is a plain list of failure cases and missing limits.
findings.source: Start here: "The three parts below say what firstmate is, follow one piece of work, and say what happens when something fails"
